transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-06
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Dr. Aaron Cole (CTO, Ridgewell), Meera (Platform), Liam (InfoSec), Sofia (DevOps)

Summary (auto): Kickoff for activation and security onboarding. Some audio dropouts in the middle, a couple of words mis-transcribed.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick round of intros, and then we'll jump straight into SSO and networking.
[00:18] Dr. Aaron Cole: thanks, maya. we've been looking forward to this. we want to make sure the inference endpoints comply with our audit controls and that PII never leaves our region.
[00:32] Jordan: cool. ops — i'll cover the private deployment options and the bench plan. just a heads up, i might say Redwood Dedicate or Redwood Dedica mess, it's the same Dedicated product — transcription sometimes munges it.
[00:47] Meera: fair, and just so you know our stack is mostly k8s on aws, with strict egress and a VPC peering requirement.
[00:58] Liam: and info sec is requiring KMS integration for key rotation and an audit trail to satisfy our internal SOC2 controls.
[01:10] Maya: absolutely — we support KMS and HSM integrations, and we can provide the full audit logs. i'll drop the SOC2 + ISO docs after the call.
[01:25] Jordan: for the deployment choices, we saw two patterns that fit most customers: "hosted with private networking" — you keep control over keys and we encrypt at rest — or "dedicated" — reserved GPU pools in a customer-dedicated tenancy with stricter isolation. each has tradeoffs in latency and cost.
[01:46] Sofia: are there measurable latency diffs between hosted and dedicated? our models are sensitive; sub-100ms is preferable for real-time assistants.
[01:58] Jordan: right — typical numbers depend on batching and sequence length. in our benchmarks, hosted gives ~70-120ms for small models but with noisy multi-tenant variance; dedicated tends to be more stable, often 50-90ms. caveat: depends on model & tokenization, and these are for 8k context small med models.
[02:20] Dr. Aaron Cole: hmm ok. cost wise, do we get committed discounts for dedicated?
[02:28] Maya: yes, there's reserved capacity pricing with monthly or annual commits — i'll include the pricing tiers in the follow-up.
[02:36] Meera: on the security front, we need SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning. anyone integrated SSO with Okta lately?
[02:46] Priya: yes — we have a standard SAML SSO flow and SCIM for user provisioning, and it's usually a straightforward exchange of metadata. we also support role-based access controls (RBAC) per team.
[02:58] Liam: will audit logs show token-level access? we need to tie requests to service accounts.
[03:06] Jordan: logs are token-level with request IDs, and we can route logs to your cloud logging or syslog via secure forwarding. sometimes the transcript will say "token level" as "tocken level", just FYI.
[03:20] Maya: next, pilot scope. what are the top three use-cases you want to validate in the pilot?
[03:29] Dr. Aaron Cole: two priorities: a clinician-facing summarization flow for internal notes, and a customer-facing chat summarizer embedded in our patient portal. third is an embed/semantic search for research documents.
[03:42] Meera: for the summaries, we'd like max latency of 150ms on most queries, 99th percentile under 350ms. is that realistic?
[03:52] Jordan: 150ms avg might be tight depending on prompt length and batch size; we can get close with aggressive batching and KV cache priming for repeated prefixes. the 99th under 350ms is achievable on Dedicated with node pinning and pre-warmed KV caches.
[04:14] Dr. Aaron Cole: cool. can you simulate KV cache hit rates? our workflows have heavy prefix reuse.
[04:21] Jordan: yes — we'll include cache-hit simulations in the bench run. i'll approximate a 60-80% hit scenario unless you give us real traces.
[04:33] Sofia: i can scrub and share representative traces — how do you want them formatted?
[04:38] Jordan: plain JSON or ndjson with timestamp, prompt hash, and session id is best. please mask PHI — we don't need raw PII.
[04:50] Priya: action items — i'll set cadence and share the onboarding playbook. the playbook includes runbook for VPC peering and SSO steps.
[04:59] Liam: on KMS, vendor-wise we prefer AWS KMS, but we also have an HSM in the future. do you have HSM connectors?
[05:07] Jordan: yes — we support AWS KMS and bring-your-own-HSM via customer HSM connectors for on-prem keys. we'll note that in the security packet.
[05:18] Dr. Aaron Cole: another question on data residency: if we deploy in eu-west-1 and restrict egress, does Redwood provide proof of data locality?
[05:27] Maya: yes — we can provide region-scoped deployments and attestations for data residency; our private deployments let you pin the region and we can disable cross-region backups if required.
[05:40] Meera: regarding network, do you require full VPC peering or do you support PrivateLink-type setups?
[05:47] Jordan: both. we support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink for more conservative network topologies. for peering we usually provide a CloudFormation template to simplify the setup.
[05:58] Sofia: ok we'll prefer PrivateLink for minimal blast radius.
[06:02] Maya: great. i'll mark that preference.
[06:10] -- mid-call note: audio crackle for ~20s, some words dropped --
[20:34] Jordan: (resuming) i'm showing the architecture slide — the runtime does KV caching, batching and smart routing. for your workloads, we'd probably recommend a small dedicated pool to start plus hosted fallback for overflow.
[20:46] Dr. Aaron Cole: okay, scale plan? if we ramp to 500 rps, what does that look like?
[20:51] Jordan: 500 rps sustained is a medium-sized commit; we'd size the GPU fleet accordingly and recommend autoscale headroom. for pilot let's target 50-100 rps to validate latencies.
[21:05] Meera: do you have a recommended metric dashboard? prometheus compatible?
[21:11] Jordan: yes — we expose metrics and traces; we have a Grafana dashboard template you can import, and traces include per-token timings and batch sizes.
[21:22] Liam: and for compliance, will you sign a DPA and provide subprocessor list?
[21:27] Maya: yes; i'll include the DPA and subprocessor list in the packet and the security contact.
[21:35] Dr. Aaron Cole: thanks. can you also show us the dedicated rollout plan? including canary, rollback?
[21:43] Jordan: absolutely — we support canary rollouts, A/B splits and automatic fallback to hosted variants. we'll provide the runbook steps.
[21:53] Sofia: who do we spam if something goes down in pilot outside hours?
[21:58] Priya: we'll set up an on-call rotation and a dedicated slack channel; for Dedicated customers there's a pager rota option with 24/7 escalation.
[22:09] Dr. Aaron Cole: cool. timebox check — we have about 25 minutes left to go through bench details and scheduling.
[22:16] Jordan: quick bench plan: SE will run 10k-message pass with your scrubbed traces, measure p50/p95/p99, token cost estimates, and cache-hit delta. we'll provide a spreadsheet with assumptions.
[22:29] Meera: what about model versions and quantization — we use an Llama2 derivative internally.
[22:36] Jordan: we support most open variants; quantized variants can reduce cost dramatically but we should validate quality. we'll include quantization notes and recommended model variants based on your prompt set.
[22:49] Dr. Aaron Cole: competitor question — has anyone talked to Anthropic? we want to compare hallucination controls and safety nets.
[22:57] Maya: yes, competitors mentioned in the space; we can add a short comparison doc but we focus on production economics: predictable latency, cache, and routing controls that keep cost down.
[23:10] Liam: ok, that helps.
[23:15] -- last 10 minutes: recap and next steps --
[38:40] Priya: recap: Redwood will send security packet (SOC2/ISO/DPA), pricing tiers, and Dedicated/reserved capacity options; SE will run bench with sample traces; schedule private networking walkthrough; set weekly standup.
[38:58] Maya: anything else?
[39:05] Dr. Aaron Cole: please include a note on SLA for Dedicated and data retention windows.
[39:12] Maya: yes — will include SLA targets and retention configs.
[39:18] Sofia: timeline: we want pilot kickoff in two weeks if possible.
[39:23] Priya: sounds feasible if traces come this week.
[39:28] Maya: great. i'll follow up with a calendar for the VPC walkthrough and attach the docs.
[39:34] Dr. Aaron Cole: thanks everyone.
[39:36] Maya: thanks, talk soon.
